description: Expected results for the official OpenFOAM tutorial tutorials/incompressibleFluid/cavity (OpenFOAM Foundation, OpenFOAM-dev git d41922f7): lid-driven square cavity, 20x20x1 cells, lid speed 1 m/s, nu 1e-5 m2/s, k-epsilon RAS, foamRun (incompressibleFluid) from t=0 to t=10 s with dt=0.005 s, writing every 0.5 s. inputs/ are the unmodified files from the OpenFOAM git tree (git show HEAD). Values are the fields at t=10 s. No reference output ships with this tutorial, so values were recorded from real runs of the server's build; two clean runs gave byte-identical output in every time folder (deterministic).

numeric_checks.name: U_mag_mean
numeric_checks.why: mean cell speed at t=10 s (m/s)

numeric_checks.name: U_mag_max
numeric_checks.why: max cell speed at t=10 s (m/s), below the lid speed 1

numeric_checks.name: p_mean
numeric_checks.why: mean kinematic pressure at t=10 s (m2/s2)

numeric_checks.name: p_min
numeric_checks.why: min kinematic pressure (vortex core / low corner)

numeric_checks.name: p_max
numeric_checks.why: max kinematic pressure (lid corner where the flow hits the wall)

numeric_checks.name: k_mean
numeric_checks.why: mean turbulent kinetic energy at t=10 s (m2/s2)

numeric_checks.name: k_max
numeric_checks.why: max turbulent kinetic energy at t=10 s

numeric_checks.name: epsilon_mean
numeric_checks.why: mean dissipation rate at t=10 s (m2/s3)

numeric_checks.name: nut_mean
numeric_checks.why: mean turbulent viscosity at t=10 s (m2/s)

numeric_checks.name: courant_max
numeric_checks.why: max Courant number of the last time step

extra_checks: foamRun return code 0 and its log ends with 'End' (OpenFOAM's normal finish line)
every final residual of the last step < 1e-3 (KI run tool threshold)
recorded_with: blockMesh + foamRun from /home/server/knowledge-dissection-toolkit/auto_dissect/_work/OpenFOAM/source/repo/platforms/linux64GccDPInt32Opt/bin (env from its etc/bashrc); foamRun run through the KI tools/run_openfoam.py, fields read through the KI tools/parse_openfoam_output.py
reference: None ships with the tutorial. The well-known Ghia et al. (1982) centreline data is for laminar Re=100 on fine grids and is not part of OpenFOAM, so it is not used.
notes: Tolerances are loose against the exact repeat (identical bytes) so that a rebuild with another compiler still passes; a change in the physics would move these numbers by far more.
